about.title: Alturas Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Alturas is small enough that a death touches nearly everyone. In a town of about 2,594 people, the county seat of Modoc County, the person who did not come home was likely a neighbor, a coworker, or someone you saw every week on 4th Street. When that loss was caused by someone else's carelessness — a driver on County Road 1 or County Road 54, an unsafe worksite, a medical mistake, a hazard a property owner ignored — California law gives certain family members the right to bring a civil wrongful death claim. The most recent final crash year, 2025, recorded zero injury collisions and zero traffic deaths inside Alturas. That does not make a family's loss any less real, and it does not mean wrongful death only follows a crash. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match Modoc County families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. You tell us what happened; a lawyer explains where things stand.

whyChoose.title: What an Independent Attorney Brings to a Modoc County Wrongful Death Case

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other situations. An attorney sorts this out early so the right people are named from the start.

items.title: The two-year deadline, watched closely
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death to file, and the window is shorter when a government entity — a county road crew, a public vehicle — is involved. An attorney tracks those dates so grief does not quietly cost you the claim.

items.title: A full picture of recoverable losses
items.desc: Recoverable losses in California include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. An attorney documents each of these rather than letting an insurer define the loss.

items.question: There were no recorded traffic deaths in Alturas in 2025. Can my family still have a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Yes. Public collision records for Alturas show zero traffic deaths in the most recent final year, but wrongful death claims are not limited to crashes. A death tied to a ranch or workplace incident, a medical error, a fall on unsafe property, or a defective product can also give rise to a civil claim. An independent attorney can look at the specific facts and tell you whether the law applies.

items.question: The other driver is being prosecuted in Modoc County. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs separately from any criminal case brought by the district attorney. The criminal case decides punishment; the civil case addresses your family's losses. Waiting can be risky because the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court.

items.question: Who in our family is actually allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California places a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first in line. If there is no one in that group, certain dependents and heirs may have standing instead. Because the rules turn on your specific family situation, an attorney will usually confirm eligibility before anything is filed.
